DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive Arthritis (formerly Reiter's syndrome).

The clinical triad of asymmetric oligoarthritis (affecting the knee and previously the ankle), urethritis (pain with urination), and the history of a prior joint attack is classic for reactive arthritis. The lack of response to standard anti-gonococcal or anti-streptococcal testing, combined with the specific pattern of monoarthritis and urinary symptoms, supports this diagnosis.
